from ./Foliage import Foliage

export anchor Lod:
    description:
        Every variant has three levels of detail built from the same skeleton.
        Foliage does not change level: its sprites thin out continuously
        (@{Foliage.simplification}). Branch levels and the impostor change by a
        cross-fade, never a swap.

    levels:
        - LOD0 is the full skeleton as tapered branch tubes whose radial segment count falls with branch order. Twigs below a species radius are left out; the foliage sprites cover them.
        - LOD1 keeps only the trunk and the first-order limbs. The finer branches it drops sit inside the crown, so the sprites hide the change.
        - LOD2 is an octahedral impostor baked from LOD0 with its full foliage, with albedo, normal, depth and thickness, lit by the same lit path, sun, sky, fog and shadows as the geometry. It is never drawn with albedo alone.

from ./Foliage import Foliage
from ./Lod import Lod
from ./Performance import Performance

export anchor Drawing:
    description:
        Trees are opaque geometry and are ordered by the depth buffer alone.
        What is in front is decided per pixel by the depth test, never by the
        order in which trees, sprites or instances are submitted, so trees
        never draw over things in front of them or vanish behind things
        behind them.

    passes:
        - Every tree level, the branch levels, the foliage sprites and the impostor, draws in the game's opaque pass with the terrain, before any transparent pass such as dust, spray, smoke, water, glass, particles or the HUD. Trees are never put in a transparent or sorted queue, so transparent effects always draw over them by their own rules.
        - Sprites, instances and batches are never sorted by distance and need not be. The picture is the same whatever order they are submitted in, including whatever order GPU culling compacts them into (@{Performance.mitigations}).
        - Order inside the opaque pass: the depth-only pass for the foliage sprites first, then the lit pass of every tree level.

    depth:
        - Tree passes use the game's camera projection, near and far planes, depth range and depth convention, including reversed depth if the game uses it, and the depth test that convention calls for. No tree pass turns depth testing off, writes depth with a different comparison, or uses its own projection.
        - Every tree level writes depth. The alpha test discards a pixel before it writes depth, in the depth-only pass and the shadow pass too, so the holes between leaves never hide what is behind them.
        - The lit pass for sprites tests for equal depth only because every pass computes their positions with the same function (@{Foliage.wind}). The vertex position output is marked invariant, or the equivalent, so the compiler cannot compute it differently in two passes. If the renderer cannot guarantee that, the prepass is dropped and sprites draw once, alpha-tested, with the normal depth test.
        - A sprite quad is centred on its cluster, so sprites in front of the trunk hide it and sprites behind are hidden by it.
        - The impostor writes a per-pixel depth from its baked depth map, so it meets the terrain and neighbouring trees where the tree would, not as a flat card. Its quad sits at the front of the tree's bounding sphere and the written depth only ever moves away from the camera, so conservative depth keeps early depth testing on.
        - Both levels in a fade (@{Lod.transition}) write their own depth through the dither, so neither draws over the other.
        - The trunk's base is sunk below the terrain by the base radius, so the tree never shares a surface with the ground and never z-fights with it.

    culling: Occlusion culling is two-phase. Trees hidden by the previous frame's depth are tested again against this frame's depth after the first draw, and drawn if visible, so a tree coming out from behind a hill or a closer tree never appears a frame late or flickers.

    debug: The @{Lod.debugView} toggle can also show tree depth, and mark pixels where a sprite's lit pass failed the equal-depth test against its own depth pass.

from ./Foliage import Foliage
from ./Grammar import Grammar
from ./Lod import Lod
from ./Performance import Performance
from ./Placement import Placement
from ./Species import Species

export anchor ProceduralTrees:
    description:
        Every tree in the rally game is generated procedurally from a
        parametric, stochastic, bracketed L-system. The hand-made tree
        assets the game used before are replaced and no longer loaded or
        placed anywhere. One generated branch skeleton per tree variant is
        the single source for every level of detail, for its foliage, its
        wind animation and its collision, so all of them agree with each
        other.

    pipeline:
        - The species definition and a seed are expanded by the grammar into a symbol string (@{Grammar}).
        - A turtle interprets the string into a branch skeleton and leaf attachment points.
        - The skeleton is meshed into every LOD, foliage sprites are placed on its leaf points, and the impostor is baked from the full-detail tree (@{Lod}, @{Foliage}).
        - Trees are placed along the stage and drawn as instances of a small pool of variants per species (@{Placement}).
        - What all of this costs at load and per frame is measured in the game (@{Performance}).

    species: Tree kinds are data, not code; see @{Species}.

    integration:
        - The tree system is built inside the game's existing codebase, in its language, on its renderer, and reads its stage data, collision, camera and graphics quality settings. It adds no second engine or renderer.
        - The tree system is one module with stages for grammar, skeleton, meshing, impostor baking, placement and drawing, in that order. Each stage only reads the output of the stages before it.
        - Grammar derivation and skeleton building are pure functions of the species and the seed, with no engine dependency, so they can be unit tested on their own.
        - The old tree assets and the code that loaded and placed them are removed, not left behind a switch.

    goals:
        - LOD changes are not visible as pops: the silhouette, crown volume, colour and lighting of a tree stay continuous while it changes level.
        - Foliage reads as clustered leaves on real branches, lit from both sides and moving in the wind, not as flat cards stuck on a trunk.
        - The same stage always grows the same trees, on every machine and in every replay.

        parametric, stochastic, bracketed L-system. The hand-made tree
        assets the game used before are replaced and no longer loaded or
        placed anywhere. One generated branch skeleton per tree variant is
        the single source for every level of detail, for its foliage, its
        wind animation and its collision, so all of them agree with each
        other.

    pipeline:
        - The species definition and a seed are expanded by the grammar into a symbol string (@{Grammar}).
        - A turtle interprets the string into a branch skeleton and leaf attachment points.
        - The skeleton is meshed into every LOD, foliage sprites are placed on its leaf points, and the impostor is baked from the full-detail tree (@{Lod}, @{Foliage}).
        - Trees are placed along the stage and drawn as instances of a small pool of variants per species (@{Placement}).
        - They draw as opaque geometry, ordered by the depth buffer alone (@{Drawing}).
        - What all of this costs at load and per frame is measured in the game (@{Performance}).

    species: Tree kinds are data, not code; see @{Species}.

    integration:
        - The tree system is built inside the game's existing codebase, in its language, on its renderer, and reads its stage data, collision, camera and graphics quality settings. It adds no second engine or renderer.
        - The tree system is one module with stages for grammar, skeleton, meshing, impostor baking, placement and drawing, in that order. Each stage only reads the output of the stages before it.
        - Grammar derivation and skeleton building are pure functions of the species and the seed, with no engine dependency, so they can be unit tested on their own.
        - The old tree assets and the code that loaded and placed them are removed, not left behind a switch.

    goals:
        - LOD changes are not visible as pops: the silhouette, crown volume, colour and lighting of a tree stay continuous while it changes level.
        - Foliage reads as clustered leaves on real branches, lit from both sides and moving in the wind, not as flat cards stuck on a trunk.
        - The same stage always grows the same trees, on every machine and in every replay.

# Drawing

## Description

Trees are opaque geometry and are ordered by the depth buffer alone. What is in front is decided per pixel by the depth test, never by the order in which trees, sprites or instances are submitted, so trees never draw over things in front of them or vanish behind things behind them.

## Passes

- Every tree level, the branch levels, the foliage sprites and the impostor, draws in the game's opaque pass with the terrain, before any transparent pass such as dust, spray, smoke, water, glass, particles or the HUD. Trees are never put in a transparent or sorted queue, so transparent effects always draw over them by their own rules.
- Sprites, instances and batches are never sorted by distance and need not be. The picture is the same whatever order they are submitted in, including whatever order GPU culling compacts them into ([Performance.mitigations](./Performance.md#mitigations)).
- Order inside the opaque pass: the depth-only pass for the foliage sprites first, then the lit pass of every tree level.

## Depth

- Tree passes use the game's camera projection, near and far planes, depth range and depth convention, including reversed depth if the game uses it, and the depth test that convention calls for. No tree pass turns depth testing off, writes depth with a different comparison, or uses its own projection.
- Every tree level writes depth. The alpha test discards a pixel before it writes depth, in the depth-only pass and the shadow pass too, so the holes between leaves never hide what is behind them.
- The lit pass for sprites tests for equal depth only because every pass computes their positions with the same function ([Foliage.wind](./Foliage.md#wind)). The vertex position output is marked invariant, or the equivalent, so the compiler cannot compute it differently in two passes. If the renderer cannot guarantee that, the prepass is dropped and sprites draw once, alpha-tested, with the normal depth test.
- A sprite quad is centred on its cluster, so sprites in front of the trunk hide it and sprites behind are hidden by it.
- The impostor writes a per-pixel depth from its baked depth map, so it meets the terrain and neighbouring trees where the tree would, not as a flat card. Its quad sits at the front of the tree's bounding sphere and the written depth only ever moves away from the camera, so conservative depth keeps early depth testing on.
- Both levels in a fade ([Lod.transition](./Lod.md#transition)) write their own depth through the dither, so neither draws over the other.
- The trunk's base is sunk below the terrain by the base radius, so the tree never shares a surface with the ground and never z-fights with it.

## Culling

Occlusion culling is two-phase. Trees hidden by the previous frame's depth are tested again against this frame's depth after the first draw, and drawn if visible, so a tree coming out from behind a hill or a closer tree never appears a frame late or flickers.

## Debug

The [Lod.debugView](./Lod.md#debug-view) toggle can also show tree depth, and mark pixels where a sprite's lit pass failed the equal-depth test against its own depth pass.
13:- They draw as opaque geometry, ordered by the depth buffer alone ([Drawing](./Drawing.md#drawing)).

I've added a spec for how trees are drawn. Every tree is opaque geometry, and what appears in front is decided by the depth buffer, never by the order things are drawn in. I couldn't look at the actual bug because `src/` is still empty here, so each rule targets a likely cause. `piton check` and `piton build` both pass.

**Likely causes, and the rule that rules each one out:**

| Likely cause | Rule now in the spec |
| --- | --- |
| Trees or sprites in a transparent or sorted queue, or drawn after dust, spray or water | Every tree level draws in the opaque pass with the terrain, before anything transparent. Nothing in the trees is sorted by distance. |
| Tree passes using their own projection or depth range, or the wrong test for reversed depth | Trees use the game's projection, near and far planes and depth convention. No tree pass turns depth testing off. |
| Gaps between leaves still writing depth, so they hide what's behind them | The alpha test discards a pixel before it writes depth, in every pass including shadows. |
| The lit pass failing its equal-depth test because positions differ slightly between passes | Sprite positions are marked invariant so every pass computes them identically. If the renderer can't guarantee that, the depth pre-pass is dropped. |
| Impostors sorting against the terrain and nearby trees as a flat card | The impostor writes depth per pixel from its baked depth map, set up so early depth testing stays on. |
| Trunk base flickering against the ground (z-fighting) | The base of the trunk is sunk below the terrain. |
| Trees appearing a frame late when they come out from behind a hill | Occlusion culling is two-phase: trees hidden by last frame's depth are tested again against this frame's. |

The debug view can now also show tree depth, and mark pixels where a sprite failed its equal-depth test.

**What changed in the spec:**
- **`spec/trees/Drawing.pi`** (new anchor `Drawing`): sections `passes`, `depth`, `culling` and `debug`.
- **`spec/trees/ProceduralTrees.pi`**: a `pipeline` step now links to `Drawing`.

**Anchors the code should follow:** `Drawing.passes`, `Drawing.depth`, `Drawing.culling` and `Drawing.debug` in `.claude/reference/trees/Drawing.md`, along with `Lod.transition` and `Foliage.wind`, which they rely on. The code step should first use the new depth view to find which of these causes is the real one, then bring the tree passes in line with all of `Drawing`.
